- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% for the next 3–5 days to capture reversion.
- In high-sentiment periods (≥0.7), model often underpredicts volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% for next 7–10 days to reflect sentiment-driven risk premium.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.25) and price is near recent 10-day mean, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
